subject.title: fix(gateway): cap pendingFinalDelivery retries and prevent delivery wedge

question: Should OpenClaw permanently retire a durable pending final after ten accepted restart-recovery attempts?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well-proven, but the irreversible retention-versus-wedge tradeoff and chosen default threshold are product and operator-recovery policy that automation cannot decide.

options.title: Accept bounded retirement
options.body: Land the submitted ten-attempt exponential-backoff policy because it prevents permanent restart wedges while providing repeated delivery opportunities.

options.title: Add recoverable dead letters
options.body: Preserve exhausted payloads in an operator-visible recovery store before clearing active session state.

options.title: Reject automatic retirement
options.body: Keep durable pending finals indefinitely and pursue a different anti-wedge mechanism.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded retirement
recommendation.body: Land the submitted ten-attempt exponential-backoff policy because it prevents permanent restart wedges while providing repeated delivery opportunities.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and most recently maintained the restart-recovery module and its startup lifecycle integration.
